auditor: muse-spark-1.3 (Meta Model API), one call per section, reasoning_effort low
scope: compiled facts vs the handbook pages they cite (card backs are byte copies of these facts); exam items and lesson narration not checked in this pass

flagged.issue: The page states braking distance grows on wet, icy or gravel roads but does not state that only braking distance grows.
flagged.suggested_fix: Reaction distance is before brakes are applied and braking distance is after, and the page states braking distance grows on wet, icy or gravel roads.

flagged.issue: The cited page states the three-feet right-turn setup but does not state the within-one-foot centerline left-turn setup.
flagged.suggested_fix: A right turn sets up about three feet from the right edge of the road.

flagged.issue: The page states the sign is displayed on vehicles but does not state it is not on a post.
flagged.suggested_fix: Warning signs are usually diamond shaped and yellow or green, while the cut-cornered triangle is displayed on slow-moving vehicles such as farm vehicles.

flagged.issue: The page does not state that shape alone identifies the sign when the face is obscured.
flagged.suggested_fix: A regulatory sign is a white rectangle stating what a driver must or must not do, whereas a warning sign is usually a yellow or green diamond warning of danger.

flagged.issue: The page does not call work zone signs temporary or contrast them with permanent yellow warning diamonds.
flagged.suggested_fix: Work zone signs are orange diamonds or rectangles warning of hazards ahead, and a flagger has legal authority to control traffic and must be obeyed.

flagged.issue: Page 41 states the red-light stop rule but does not state the yellow-light prepare-to-stop rule.
flagged.suggested_fix: Cite page 40 for yellow lights preparing to stop and page 41 for red lights requiring a stop.

flagged.issue: Page 40 states the pedestrian left-side rule but does not state the bicyclist right-side rule.
flagged.suggested_fix: Limit statement to pedestrians on page 40 or also cite page 42 for bicyclists riding on the right with traffic.

flagged.issue: Page 44 states the never-go-around rule and hiding but the enter-a-blind-spot consequence is on page 45.
flagged.suggested_fix: State only that you must never go around a backing truck and trailers can hide objects.

flagged.issue: Page 45 states the mirror test for the rear blind spot but not for the side blind spots.
flagged.suggested_fix: State the mirror test only for the rear blind spot on this page.

flagged.issue: Page 45 states the orange-red triangle meaning but does not mention an orange diamond work zone.
flagged.suggested_fix: State only that the orange and red triangle identifies a slow moving vehicle.

flagged.issue: The page says 4 inches can make walking difficult and hide hazards, not that it can knock a walker down.
flagged.suggested_fix: As little as 4 inches of running water can make it difficult to walk and can obstruct hazards from view.

flagged.issue: Page 50 states the sunset/sunrise rule but does not state the 500-feet visibility rule on that page.
flagged.suggested_fix: Page 50 requires headlights a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise and when snow, rain, and fog limit visibility.

flagged.issue: Page 48 does not state better traction in snow, only lack of good traction on ice.
flagged.suggested_fix: Page 48 says even four-wheel or all-wheel drive vehicles do not have good traction on ice and to increase following distance to more than 4 seconds.

flagged.issue: The cited page excerpt does not state looking toward the right edge of the highway.
flagged.suggested_fix: Look at the highway until the bright lights have gone by and vision returns; this practice helps detect bicyclists or pedestrians near the edge.

flagged.issue: The page states white should be on the right but does not state yellow is on the left.
flagged.suggested_fix: A yellow edge line to your right means you are going the wrong way on a divided highway; the line to your right should be white.

flagged.issue: The page states the 6-month loss but does not state it is separate from DUI conviction penalties.
flagged.suggested_fix: Refusing the test costs the license for at least six months.

flagged.issue: The page does not state that coffee/shower/exercise only change how awake you feel.
flagged.suggested_fix: Only time at at least an hour per drink reduces alcohol's effects; coffee, cold showers and exercise will not sober a person up.

flagged.issue: Page 66 states the 60-day and 24-hour requirements but does not state the 30-day name/address/color change requirement.
flagged.suggested_fix: Limit this page-66 statement to the 60-day registration and 24-hour mailing requirements, and cite page 67 for the 30-day change notice.
